pages.text: It rained in the night. In the morning, a big puddle lay in the schoolyard. At break time, Delanyo jumped right over it. After lunch, he went back to look, yet the puddle was gone.
sentences: It rained in the night.
In the morning, a big puddle lay in the schoolyard.
At break time, Delanyo jumped right over it.
After lunch, he went back to look, yet the puddle was gone.
pages.alt: In a sunny Ghanaian schoolyard at morning break, Delanyo leaps cheerfully over a wide rainwater puddle while Tiwaa watches with a smile.

pages.text: “Where did the water go?” he asked. “Did it sink into the ground?” “Some of it did,” said Tiwaa, “yet the sun is hot today. Maybe the sun took some of it.” “Let us test it,” said Delanyo.
sentences: “Where did the water go?” he asked.
“Did it sink into the ground?” “Some of it did,” said Tiwaa, “yet the sun is hot today.
Maybe the sun took some of it.” “Let us test it,” said Delanyo.
pages.alt: Delanyo and Tiwaa crouching curiously beside a warm, sun-dried patch of earth in the bright schoolyard where the puddle had been.

pages.text: They poured the exact same amount of water into two matching white saucers. They placed one saucer in the bright sun and the other in the cool shade. With a pencil, they marked a neat line at the water rim on each saucer.
sentences: They poured the exact same amount of water into two matching white saucers.
They placed one saucer in the bright sun and the other in the cool shade.
With a pencil, they marked a neat line at the water rim on each saucer.
pages.alt: Tiwaa marking a thin pencil line inside one of two matching white saucers of clear water—one placed on a sunlit courtyard bench and one in the cool veranda shade.

pages.text: After two hours, they checked both saucers. The water in the sunny saucer had gone down a lot, while the water in the shady saucer had gone down only a little. “The sun makes it go faster,” said Tiwaa.
sentences: After two hours, they checked both saucers.
The water in the sunny saucer had gone down a lot, while the water in the shady saucer had gone down only a little.
“The sun makes it go faster,” said Tiwaa.
pages.alt: Delanyo and Tiwaa comparing the two white saucers side by side: the sunny saucer holds very little water below its pencil line while the shady saucer remains nearly full.

pages.text: Their teacher explained kindly, “When the sun warms water, some of it turns into a gas called water vapour. We cannot see it as it rises into the air. This change is called evaporation.”
sentences: Their teacher explained kindly, “When the sun warms water, some of it turns into a gas called water vapour.
We cannot see it as it rises into the air.
This change is called evaporation.”
pages.alt: In the sunlit schoolyard beside the saucers, their teacher gestures gently upward toward the warm sky while Delanyo and Tiwaa look up thoughtfully.

pages.text: “Wet clothes dry on a line in the exact same way,” added their teacher. “The water rises into the air. Later, high up, the vapour cools to form clouds, and rain falls again.” Delanyo grinned. “So our puddle is up in the sky!”
sentences: “Wet clothes dry on a line in the exact same way,” added their teacher.
“The water rises into the air.
Later, high up, the vapour cools to form clouds, and rain falls again.” Delanyo grinned.
“So our puddle is up in the sky!”
pages.alt: Bright Ghanaian courtyard scene with colourful washed clothes drying on a sunny washing line beneath fluffy white clouds while Delanyo and Tiwaa grin happily.

activities.question: In which saucer did the water go down faster?
What is water vapour?
options: A gas that we cannot see

activities.definition: When liquid water turns into a gas and rises into the air.

glossary.definition: A small pool of rainwater on the ground.
Water in the form of an invisible gas in the air.
When liquid water turns into a gas and goes into the air.
